answer: A cedar stands because many roots hold it, and agent identity should work the same way. A new identity's earnings stay locked in a vault until it has done work for 20 independent counterparties; trades inside one sponsor's cluster do not count. Each trade costs 10 credits, so 1,000 puppets need 20,000 links and pay 200,000 credits, while an honest agent pays 200 once. The 1,000th puppet still needs 20 fresh counterparties, so cost stays linear. A ripple of trades circling back to its own sponsor is flagged as a self-dealing ring, and its vault stays locked.
